paragraphs: Define the decision and objectives with stakeholders, validate the data, specify variables and constraints, and solve and compare alternatives. Test the model and changing inputs, explain assumptions and limitations, and work with the implementing team to review outcomes.
Mostly works in an office with cross-functional teams, using data around supply chains, public services, finance, or operations planning.

Operations research emphasizes objectives, constraints and models for operational decisions and compares implementable alternatives. It overlaps with data science, statistics and management analysis and includes validation, communication and implementation work. Approval authority depends on the organization, not the job title.

For the fictional exercise, useful outputs include a reproducible model, an input data dictionary, scenario comparisons and decision notes. These are editorial learning examples, not universal employer standards.

The work combines mathematical modeling and data validation with explaining conflicting objectives, identifying infeasible constraints and communicating with business and implementation teams. A successful solve does not establish that the problem was defined correctly.
These occupations can overlap in data, methods and implementation. Compare the actual problem, output and preparation rather than assuming an exclusive boundary or transferable authorization.
The comparison uses each occupation’s O*NET definition and selected tasks. These descriptions do not establish admission rules, transfer distance or a success rate.
Compare operations research with six related occupations by their typical work and outputs. Similar titles or shared tools are only starting points for exploration.
Data science may include prediction and optimization; operations research focuses on comparing decisions under objectives and constraints, with overlap.
Explore data science if feature analysis, prediction or analytical applications interest you.
Explorer
Use the stated fictional shift case to practice objectives, constraints and independent calculations. An exercise is for learning, not a competence test.
Practising analyst
Trial a tool on permitted, bounded inputs and compare its output with independent calculations and known cases. Record errors and limits instead of assuming a benefit.
Team or project lead
Clarify who confirms objectives, reviews data and models, releases changes and adopts decisions in the actual project. Use the organization’s validation and exception process.
Career changer
Compare the target role’s mathematical methods, programming, domain knowledge and collaboration tasks. Identify training gaps; a short course does not guarantee a role.

entries: Do you enjoy turning an unclear operational problem into variables and constraints that can be checked?
Are you willing to revisit data, units and records rather than pursuing only a one-off solution?
When results differ from expectations, do you keep the checks and investigate why?
After a stakeholder or colleague offers a counterexample, can you explain which assumptions or constraints need revision?
What preparation and support do stakeholder interviews and individual modeling each require?
Can written model notes and discussion check one another without treating a preferred communication style as a type-based limit?
When asked to change an objective, can you separate personal preferences, business objectives and fixed constraints?
When views conflict, can you document the disagreement and evidence for the actual decision owner?
Can you explain why shift counts are integers and identify the units in the capacity constraint?
Can you identify why the original 2B plan is infeasible for demand of 23 items?
Can you restate an implementation team’s service or capacity concern before explaining the plan?
When the model omits something, can you acknowledge it and identify missing information rather than defend the original result?

Objective mis-specification: optimizing a single cost while omitting service or fairness constraints. May make a plan unacceptable in reality. Control: review objectives and limits with the business side.
Data bias: samples are outdated or missing. May cause model output to mislead decisions. Control: perform quality checks and sensitivity analysis.
O*NET supplies task and model-validation context. Risk scenarios and actions here are editorial checks, not incident rates, legal duties or universal institutional procedures.
The model reuses historical demand, costs or capacities without checking whether current conditions still match.

When critical data remain unverified, objectives or constraints are disputed, or results fall outside the validated scope, record the affected conclusions and refer them to the actual project owner. Any suspension of real operations follows the risk and applicable procedure.

Fictional paper case: compare the stated shift combinations without real clients, routes or operations. Problem statement: 20 items must be delivered in one day; full shift A has a capacity of 12 items and a cost of CNY 100, full shift B has a capacity of 10 items and a cost of CNY 90, each with at most 2 shifts, partial loading is allowed, cost is independent of load, and the number of shifts is a non-negative integer. Compare total cost only across the three cases A+B, 2A, and 2B, list capacity and unused capacity, then change demand to 23 items and re-check; do not call the best of the three candidates a true business global optimum. Unprovided distances, delivery windows, staffing and fairness requirements are not assumed absent. This case does not establish real delivery feasibility or personal occupational competence.

BLS describes typical U.S. entry as at least a bachelor’s degree; some employers require or prefer a master’s. Mathematics, programming and domain knowledge need practical development. Check the actual role rather than treating a course or degree as data access, release or decision authority.

Reference delivery: with 20 items, A+B has capacity 22, cost CNY 190, unused 2; 2A has capacity 24, cost CNY 200, unused 4; 2B has capacity 20, cost CNY 180, unused 0; all three cases are feasible and 2B is the lowest. With demand 23, only 2A with capacity 24 is feasible, costing CNY 200 with unused 1; the original low-cost plan fails. Submit the data dictionary, the feasibility and cost table for the three cases, demand sensitivity, and a note on omitted time windows/routes/fairness limits. Mathematical training does not equal real scheduling approval authority. This demonstrates calculations and explanations for the stated model, not real data judgment, stakeholder negotiation or occupational competence, and it grants no scheduling authority.

details: Editorial scenario index: three restricted information outputs are equally weighted; floor((50+75+75)/3+0.5)=67. It is not a measured proportion of all occupational tasks.

Rating 50 assumes substantial assistance with considerable clarification and revision. Rating 75 assumes that most of an information draft can be formed with complete given inputs and rules and checked afterwards. These are editorial assumptions, not measured occupational effects.

50/100: organize objectives, capacities, costs and service requirements already confirmed by stakeholders into candidate objective and constraint lists. The tool does not choose their values or invent limits; task_rows[0].

75/100: draft variables, capacity constraints and enumeration code only for the fully specified integer-shift case on this page. Check them against reference arithmetic and feasible/infeasible cases. This is not a capability percentage for arbitrary real optimization models; task_rows[2].

75/100: draft feasibility, cost comparisons and notes only for the three given candidates and demands of 20/23 items. Recalculate each result; do not claim unknown routes or a real-business global optimum; task_rows[3].
entries.limitation: 67 summarizes assumed scenario ratings. Rating reliability, occupational representativeness, actual time savings and output quality have not been validated. Real data, model release and decisions follow organizational validation, access and decision procedures.

rows.核心工作与产出: Extract, interpret and report information from structured or unstructured data using methods such as data mining and machine learning.

rows.关键区别: Statistical work can support decisions; compare collection and inference questions with operational decision modeling, without an exclusive boundary.
rows.更适合什么选择: Explore statistical work if study design, estimation and uncertainty interest you.
rows.核心工作与产出: Develop or apply statistical methods to collect, organize and interpret numerical data.

rows.关键区别: Management analysts also analyze data and support implementation; compare the project and output, not a reporting-versus-modeling divide.
rows.更适合什么选择: Explore management analysis if interviews, process evaluation and organizational improvement interest you.
rows.核心工作与产出: Study organizations and procedures and recommend improvements to systems, processes or organization.

rows.关键区别: Logisticians may redesign material flows; compare ongoing coordination with mathematical decision modeling, allowing overlap.
rows.更适合什么选择: Explore logistics if material flows and coordination with customers and suppliers interest you.
rows.核心工作与产出: Analyze and coordinate ongoing logistics, including acquisition, allocation and delivery.

rows.关键区别: Mathematicians do both theoretical and applied work; compare the mathematical question and operational decision output rather than assuming purely theoretical work.
rows.更适合什么选择: Explore mathematical work if methods themselves and applications across fields interest you.
rows.核心工作与产出: Research fundamental mathematics or apply mathematical methods to science, management and other fields.

rows.关键区别: Industrial engineering also uses optimization and statistics; compare the production system and project, without inferring site work or implementation from the title.
rows.更适合什么选择: Explore industrial engineering if production systems, human factors and engineering evaluation interest you.
rows.核心工作与产出: Design, test and evaluate production systems involving people, quality, inventory, logistics and cost.

questions.answer: State the decision in one sentence, separate objectives from hard constraints, and list questions for stakeholders.
questions.question: Am I willing to perform problem definition?

questions.answer: Record each input’s unit, source and time window, including how missing values affect the plan.
questions.question: Am I willing to perform data verification?

questions.answer: Start with the integer-shift case and check variables and constraints; successful execution does not establish correctness.
questions.question: Am I willing to perform model building?

questions.answer: Separate feasibility from cost and explain why a candidate is preferred among the three given cases.
questions.question: Am I willing to perform scenario solving?

questions.answer: Change demand from 20 to 23 and explain which plans fail rather than reporting only a new answer.
questions.question: Am I willing to perform sensitivity testing?

questions.answer: Explain assumptions, the recommendation and unresolved limits in a paragraph without solver jargon.
questions.question: Am I willing to perform results communication?

questions.answer: Without a real project, describe which predicted and observed measures you would compare; do not invent implementation results.
questions.question: Am I willing to perform deployment review?

questions.answer: Document conflicts among cost, service and fairness for the actual objective owner to consider.
questions.question: Can I handle objective mis-specification?

questions.answer: Check time windows, missingness and source differences before deciding what needs recalculation or restricted use.
questions.question: Can I handle data bias?

questions.answer: Ask the implementation team to check capacity, timing and business rules; unprovided limits cannot be assumed absent.
questions.question: Can I handle omitted constraints?

riasec_fit_block.fit_interest: Consider whether mathematical problem exploration and orderly data work interest you; observe actual learning and project feedback separately.
riasec_fit_block.interest: O*NET gives this occupation the interest code IC. Investigative clues can relate to exploring mathematical problems, while Conventional clues can relate to organizing data and information through procedures. These describe occupational activities, not required personal scores or proof of modeling or decision-making competence.
riasec_fit_block.riasec: An interest match is an exploration clue, not a substitute for mathematical training, project feedback or data permissions.
